messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: generated quantities block executed only for saved samples
parts:
This post concerns a pretty fundamental language
design decision, so please chime in if you have
an opinion!
On 3/1/13 11:17 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Actually, this [print in generated quantities] is not work
> well for Stan during the warmup phase if the warmup sample is not saved.

It's a feature, not a bug :-)

The generated quantities block is only executed for
saved samples. (It can't affect the parameters sampled.)

In particular, the generated quantities block is not called
during warmup if warmup samples are not saved and it is not
called for thinned samples.

We could change that behavior and call it all the time,
even for samples that aren't saved.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: final checklist for 1.2 release?
parts:
On Friday, March 1, 2013 10:14:12 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Is there anything else we need (or want) to do for this
release?

I don't think we should delay v1.2 for this alone, but much of the code in the examples section of the rstan package is wrapped inside a \dontrun block, which means it is not run when a user executes example(foo). The reason for this is that it would take a relatively long time to compile and run a model in order to illustrate the behavior, but it has the downside that the code in the examples section is not actually tested and is generally less useful to the user.

What I do in the mi package is to cache the output of a simple but general model, save it to R/sysdata.rda, and then load it with a comment in the examples section to illustrate the function being documented. The sysdata.rda file is mentioned at

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-subdirectories

So, with rstan it would be something like this in R

require(rstan)
dogs <- stan_demo("dogs", save_dso = FALSE)
save(dogs, file = "STAN_HOME/rstan/rstan/R/sysdata.rda", compress = "xz")

then in a shell

git add rstan/rstan/R/sysdata.rda
git commit -m "update sysdata.rda"

then in all the relevant manpages remove the \dontrun braces and insert

dogs <- rstan:::dogs # cache of stan_demo("dogs")

then whatever function is being documented can use this object to illustrate plots, etc.

This works well, but we have to remember to recache every time the format of a stanfit object changes.

Ben

messages.subject: doc & behavior of CDFs?
parts:
On 3/1/13 11:27 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> I'll have the rest of the univariate distributions gradients done this weekend. That's the last thing on my list for 1.2
>
> Regarding cdfs, the ones Michael have written have been:
> - unit tested
> - added to the language (function_signatures.hpp)
> - model tested (in src/test/gm/model_specs/compiled)
> - added to the doc

Fantastic progress!


I finally took a look at some of this code and I'm
a bit confused about what's going on with the definitions
and error checking. Maybe I'm missing something, but I
have the following questions and remaining to-do items.


0. There are tab chars in the CDF code. Looks like we need to
script another eradication. Can everyone verify that the
environment they're using for text gets rid of tabs? I just
went through mine and it looks like I'm not the culprit this time.


1. What was the final decision on the domains of the cdfs?
Do they return 0 for values below the support of the density/mass
function and to 1 for values above the support?


2. In Bernoulli CDF, I see this:

// Ensure non-zero argument lenghts
if (!(stan::length(n) && stan::length(theta)))
return 0.0;

Why return 0? I'd have thought 1.0 would be a better
boundary condition here if we don't want to raise an
error. The reason is that it's the appropriate unit to
ground out the recursion because values are multiplied,
not added.


3. I take it the propto for CDFs are just there to let us
avoid calculating them when we don't want to for truncated models?
That is, if we have

y ~ normal(0,1) T[0,]

we don't really need to calculate the cdfs. We should still
calculate the constraints, though.

In practice, for Bernoulli CDF, I see this:

// Return if everything is constant and only proportionality is required
if (!include_summand<propto,T_prob>::value)
return 0.0;

Why 0? This also seems like it should be 1.0 for the same
reason as above. As is, I think it will do the wrong thing for
a truncated model, as in:

y ~ normal(0,1) T[0,];

This would effectively return 0 probability because the
include_summand metaprogram will evaluate to false.


4. The ones remaining to be coded(?)/tested(?)/documented
are:

uniform_cdf [not that we want to encourage this one for truncation!]
binomial_logit_cdf
hypergeometric_cdf [very low priority]
ordered_logitistc_cdf
poisson_log_cdf
cauchy_cdf
double_exponential_cdf
chi_square_cdf
gamma_cdf


5. I'd eventually like to get the CDF formulas into the doc along
with their support and formulas. I'll work on that.
I'd really like to get gradients in for everything. I think it'll be
a useful general feature of our doc for people implementing other
things directly.

- Bob

parts:

On Sat, Mar 2, 2013 at 2:25 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

This post concerns a pretty fundamental language
design decision, so please chime in if you have
an opinion!

On 3/1/13 11:17 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Actually, this [print in generated quantities] is not work
well for Stan during the warmup phase if the warmup sample is not saved.

It's a feature, not a bug :-)

The generated quantities block is only executed for
saved samples.  (It can't affect the parameters sampled.)

In particular, the generated quantities block is not called
during warmup if warmup samples are not saved and it is not
called for thinned samples.

We could change that behavior and call it all the time,
even for samples that aren't saved.
- Bob

as of de5b928c1cab2da397f43a297ec1427103102040 whenever you want to v1.2.0 to drop as long as there are no more changes to the docs.

Ben
